proposals: PNGRB should publish, in its monthly natural-gas pipeline report, a capacity-weighted national utilisation figure and the utilisation of each trunk line, with the method stated, so the network’s fill level is an official series rather than a chairman’s 50% remark set against IEEFA’s 41% estimate.

PNGRB should publish line-by-line utilisation for product pipelines run in self-use mode as well as for common-carrier lines, since about 70% of product-pipeline capacity is self-use and underused lines like Mathura–Delhi are otherwise visible only through a five-year-old consultant’s estimate.

PNGRB should report each year the amount credited to the Pipeline Development Reserve by each operator, and how much was reinvested and how much passed on as tariff reduction, so the 75% utilisation trigger can be judged by the money it actually moves.

PNGRB should publish a list of industrial clusters and city gas areas lying near a trunk pipeline but not connected to it by a spur, so the “missing layer of regional connectivity” it and others cite can be tracked down connection by connection.

The Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas should state the utilisation of the completed gas grid in its year-end review alongside kilometres built, so progress reports on the roughly 25,400 km network say how much of it is used as well as how much exists.
